sections.h2: Transfer on death deeds in North Carolina
sections.html:
North Carolina has no transfer on death deed. The wills chapter of the General Statutes, Chapter 31, ends with Article 11, and that article covers electronic storage of attested wills by an attorney, not deeds that pass land at death.

The idea has been proposed. Senate Bill 160 in the 2023 session would have added a new Article 11 to Chapter 31, the Uniform Real Property Transfer on Death Act, with sections numbered 31-65 through 31-82. Its last action was a referral to the Judiciary committee on February 27, 2023. A bill that stays in committee does not become law, and the 2025 session law that did add an Article 11 dealt with electronic wills.

Laws change, so ask a North Carolina attorney before relying on any deed that claims to pass a house at death without probate. A form copied from another state does not create that right here.

sections.h2: What the 2023 bill would have done
sections.html:
It would have let an owner name a beneficiary by recorded deed, with the land passing at death and no gift made during life. The main features show what North Carolina owners lack.

  • The deed stays revocable during the owner's life, even if the document says otherwise.
  • It is treated as nontestamentary, and the owner needs the same capacity required to make a will.
  • It must be recorded to be valid, and no consideration or delivery to the beneficiary is needed.
  • The beneficiary takes the land subject to liens and interests that exist at the owner's death.
  • Liability for statutory allowances and estate claims could reach the property if the probate estate fell short.

None of this is in force. For now, owners here rely on wills, trusts and joint ownership to avoid or shorten probate.

sections.h2: How real estate passes at death without that deed
sections.html:
It passes under a will or to heirs by intestacy, and probate is handled by the clerk of superior court where the owner lived. A duly probated will is what passes title to real and personal property under G.S. 31-39. That section also sets a deadline: the will must be probated or offered for probate within two years of death, or before the clerk approves the personal representative's final account if that is earlier, for it to bind lien creditors or buyers from the heirs.

Wills must follow Chapter 31. An adult of sound mind, 18 or older, may make one (G.S. 31-1). An attested will is signed by the maker and two competent witnesses. A holographic will is written entirely in the maker's own handwriting and signed. A will can also devise property to a trustee of a trust set up before death, as G.S. 31-47 describes. Anyone can leave the original with the clerk of superior court for safekeeping, and G.S. 31-11 keeps it private until the owner dies.

Land in a second county adds a step. Certified copies of the will and of the probate certificate must reach the clerk of that other county inside the same two-year window.

Each option trades speed against formality. The table summarizes what the statutes provide for each one.

North Carolina routes for passing a house at death
RouteHow it worksStatute
Attested or holographic willValid only if it meets Chapter 31; probate is needed to pass titleG.S. 31-3.2 to 31-3.4, 31-39
Self-proved willAcknowledgment by the maker and affidavits of witnesses before an officer, attached to the willG.S. 31-11.6
Devise to a trustA will may leave property to the trustee of a trust created before deathG.S. 31-47
Small estate affidavitIn an intestate estate, personal property up to $20,000, filed with the clerk 30 or more days after death, when no personal representative petition is pendingG.S. 28A-25-1

The small estate affidavit covers personal property. It cannot move a house, so do not count on it when real estate is the main asset.

sections.h2: What can go wrong when a house goes through probate
sections.html:
The biggest delay for a buyer is title that is not settled yet. A caveat challenging the will can be filed within three years after probate (G.S. 31-32), and while one is pending the clerk's order bars distributions to beneficiaries. A title company will ask whether one has been filed.

  • No personal representative yet: ask the clerk who holds authority to sign a deed for the estate.
  • Heirs disagree: ask the clerk and a title company which signatures the closing requires.
  • Liens and taxes: each recorded lien and any unpaid property tax needs a payoff figure.
  • Records in another county: a will probated elsewhere has to be filed where the land lies.

The state estate tax was repealed for deaths from January 1, 2013 forward, so no state estate return is part of the picture. Federal rules are a separate question for the estate's lawyer or accountant.

sections.h2: Recording the deed after an heir or estate signs
sections.html:
A deed from an estate or an heir goes to the register of deeds in the county where the parcel sits. G.S. 47-18 withholds protection from a conveyance against creditors and later buyers until it is registered, and ranks competing filings by the time each was registered.

Statewide fees under G.S. 161-10 start at $26 for a short deed, and the transferor owes the seller's deed tax of $1 per $500 under G.S. 105-228.30 before filing. The register's office can give you a fee sheet with page counts and any recent change.

A quick sale is possible once someone has authority to sign and the title is clear enough to close. Heirs who would rather skip repairs and showings can ask Cash Home Buyers for an as-is offer. First confirm with the clerk who serves as personal representative, then gather the will, the letters and any payoff statements for liens or property tax. Take those papers to the title company early, since it will want to see who may sign before it schedules a closing. A cash sale also skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, which removes one source of delay while the estate is still being sorted out.

faqs.q: Is a transfer on death deed valid in North Carolina?
faqs.a: No North Carolina statute authorizes one. A 2023 Senate bill proposed it and was referred to committee on February 27, 2023, and Chapter 31 does not contain the proposed article. Ask a North Carolina attorney whether the law has changed.

faqs.q: How can I leave my house to one person and avoid probate?
faqs.a: North Carolina offers no recorded beneficiary deed. A will passes title after probate, and G.S. 31-47 lets a will leave property to the trustee of a trust created before death. A lawyer can explain which structure fits your family.

faqs.q: How long does a will have to be probated?
faqs.a: A will has to be probated or offered for probate within two years of death, or before the clerk approves the final account if that comes sooner, to be effective against lien creditors and buyers from the heirs. G.S. 31-39 sets that rule.

faqs.q: Does the small estate affidavit cover real estate?
faqs.a: No, it covers personal property of up to $20,000 in an intestate estate (more for a surviving spouse who is the sole heir) under G.S. 28A-25-1. The affidavit goes to the clerk of superior court in the county where the person lived, no sooner than 30 days after death.

faqs.q: Does North Carolina charge an estate tax?
faqs.a: No. G.S. 105-32.1 through 105-32.8 were repealed for estates of people who die on or after January 1, 2013. Federal estate rules are separate.
